title: How to Choose the Right Modular Kitchen Layout for Your Home
excerpt: From L-shaped to parallel kitchens, we break down the most popular layouts and help you pick the one that suits your Indian home perfectly.
content:
Choosing the right kitchen layout is the single most important decision when designing a modular kitchen. The layout determines how efficiently you can cook, how much storage you get, and how the space feels. In Indian homes, where the kitchen is the heart of the house, this decision carries extra weight.

**L-Shaped Kitchen:** The most popular layout in Indian apartments. It fits snugly into a corner and gives you a natural work triangle between the stove, sink and refrigerator. Ideal for medium-sized kitchens (80–120 sq ft).

**Parallel Kitchen:** Two counters facing each other. Excellent for narrow but long kitchens. Very common in Delhi apartments. Gives maximum counter space.

**U-Shaped Kitchen:** Three walls of cabinets. The ultimate in storage and counter space. Best for larger homes (140 sq ft and above).

**Straight/Linear Kitchen:** One-wall layout. Good for studio apartments or open-plan homes where the kitchen is part of the living area.

At Modular Kitchen, our designers visit your home, take accurate measurements and recommend the layout that maximises your space while matching your cooking habits.
author: Rahul Sharma

title: Modular Kitchen Materials: Marine Ply vs MDF vs HDHMR — What's Best for Delhi?
excerpt: Delhi's humidity swings and hard water can wreck a cheap kitchen in years. Here's an honest guide to the materials that actually last.
content:
Material selection is where most people make costly mistakes. Attractive price tags on poor-quality materials lead to swollen shutters and rusted fittings within 3–5 years. Delhi's climate — extreme summer heat, monsoon humidity — demands materials that can handle the stress.

**Marine Plywood:** The gold standard for kitchen carcass (the box structure). It's moisture-resistant, holds screws firmly and can last 20+ years. Slightly more expensive but worth every rupee.

**MDF (Medium Density Fibreboard):** Great for painted shutters because it gives a perfectly smooth finish. However, it can swell if water seeps into edges — so proper edgebanding is essential.

**HDHMR (High Density High Moisture Resistant):** A newer option that combines the best of both. Denser than MDF, more moisture-resistant, and holds screws well. Our top recommendation for Delhi kitchens.

**Shutters:** Options include acrylic (high gloss, easy to clean), membrane/PVC (affordable, good variety), lacquered glass (premium, stunning) and thermofoil (durable, matte).

At Modular Kitchen Dwarka, we use only BWR-grade or Marine plywood for carcasses and offer a 10-year structural warranty on all our work.
author: Priya Mehta

title: Small Kitchen, Big Storage: 10 Clever Hacks for Indian Apartments
excerpt: Most Delhi flats have compact kitchens. These 10 smart storage solutions will make your small kitchen feel twice as big and twice as organised.
content:
Indian cooking involves a LOT of vessels, spices, appliances and ingredients. Managing all of this in a 60–80 sq ft kitchen is a challenge — but completely solvable with smart modular design.

**1. Tall Pantry Units:** Floor-to-ceiling units that hold everything from atta to your mixer. Use pull-out baskets inside for easy access.

**2. Corner Carousel (Magic Corner):** The dead corner space in L-shaped kitchens can be transformed with a magic corner unit — rotating shelves that bring everything to the front.

**3. Under-Sink Organiser:** Use a custom-fitted pull-out unit under the sink to store cleaning supplies, oil bottles and spare items.

**4. Wall-Mounted Spice Rack:** Indian kitchens have 20+ spices minimum. A dedicated wall-mounted spice rack keeps them visible and accessible.

**5. Drawer Dividers:** Custom dividers inside drawers prevent utensil chaos. Separate compartments for cutlery, ladles and small gadgets.

**6. Tall Appliance Garage:** A dedicated cabinet with a shutter to hide your mixer, oven toaster and air fryer — keeping counters clean.

**7. Hanging Pot Rail:** A stainless steel rail above the counter to hang pots and pans saves 2–3 cabinet shelves.

**8. Pegboard Panel:** Inside a cabinet door, a pegboard can hold spoon sets, bottle openers and small tools.

**9. Pull-Out Dustbin:** An integrated pull-out dustbin unit keeps your kitchen hygienic and hides the bin out of sight.

**10. Toe-Kick Drawers:** The space below base cabinets (the kickboard area) can be turned into shallow drawers — perfect for storing baking trays and chopping boards.
